context: The agent turns an existing bot-protection probe report (CloudFront blocking the HeadlessChrome User-Agent; first working step: stealth + UA override) into a browser recipe for playwright-cli consumers. Judge browser-recipe.json and answer.md.

checklist.name: recipe_written
checklist.description: browser-recipe.json exists in the working directory, is valid JSON, and records the probed URL https://shop.northwind-outdoor.com/.

checklist.name: consumable_shape
checklist.description: The recipe has a top-level `cliConfig` object that is a playwright-cli config (a `browser` key with `browserName` and `launchOptions`) and a top-level `stealthInitScript` field, so a consumer can write cliConfig to a --config file and the script to an initScript file.

checklist.name: ua_override
checklist.description: cliConfig.browser.launchOptions.args contains a `--user-agent=` value for a regular desktop Chrome that does not contain 'HeadlessChrome'.

checklist.name: stealth_script
checklist.description: stealthInitScript is non-empty JavaScript that, at minimum, hides navigator.webdriver (the working step used the stealth init script).

checklist.name: minimum_config
checklist.description: The recipe matches the first successful step (stealth-ua): it does not switch to system Chrome (`channel: "chrome"`) and does not request a persistent profile.

checklist.name: diagnosis
checklist.description: answer.md attributes the block to CloudFront (server: CloudFront / x-amz-cf-id / 'The request could not be satisfied') filtering on the HeadlessChrome User-Agent, citing that stealth alone still failed and adding the UA override succeeded.

checklist.name: no_invented_signals
checklist.description: Does not claim protections absent from the report (e.g. Akamai, Cloudflare, DataDome) or claim to have re-run the probe.
